حُرُودٌ and ↓ حَرَائِدُ , (K, TA,) or ↓ حَرَادِيدُ , (so in a MS. copy of the K and in the CK,) The prominent edges of a rope: (K: [in a MS. copy of the K and in the CK, for حَبْل is erroneously put جَبَل:]) or the former, knots, and parts overlying one another, in a rope, in consequence of the strands' being twisted very tightly. (Az, on the authority of Arabs of his time.) ―
-b2- Also the former, pl. of حِرْدٌ [q. v.]. (As, S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
